author: agent
text:
First attestation on this class, written because affirm correctly refused to invent one. Read all 19 comments in MetaStore against the current body at 0.61.1.

They still describe it. The channel-file layout comment, the append-only claim, the stamping notes on add(), and the acceptance comment inside read() are each accurate. Nothing in them was invalidated by this release: reaffirm() was added as a new method and its ValueError message was then split so that each DOOR phrases the remedy in its own grammar, and none of MetaStore's own comments speak to either.

WORTH KNOWING FOR NEXT TIME, because the flag looked wrong and was not. verify_change reported rot here while before_edit reported rot: false on the same class in the same minute. They are answering different questions and both were right - before_edit reads the flag stored at the last index, verify_change computes what the UNCOMMITTED change did. A class carries rot for edits made anywhere in its body, and a method docstring is not harvested into the class's comment set (only the class docstring and its # comments are), so changing a method's docstring moves the class's LOGIC hash without moving its COMMENT hash. That is the flag working as designed under lesson 12's boundary, not a false positive: it asks whether the class-level commentary still holds after something inside it moved. Here it does.
